---
title: "Optimised Glider II"
---

A chronological record of questions asked about a 300 mm span foam glider optimised for minimum sink rate in trimmed glide. Each **chapter**
is one model — a vehicle, a fidelity, a method — and each **entry** is one
question asked of it, answered by code that runs when the page renders.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Initial user specifications

True of every chapter, and inherited by any new one:

1. **Span**: 300 mm, fixed tip to tip.
2. **Construction**: flat foam sheet, cut and assembled by hand.
3. **Objective**: minimum sink rate in trimmed glide.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Initial assumptions

1. **Still air**, no thermals and no wind gradient.
2. **Rigid airframe**, no aeroelastic deflection under load.
:::

## How the chapters relate

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# GENERATED FROM THE CHAPTERS, never drawn by hand (rule 34 keeps this block).
#
# Reads source, executes none of it: no chapter model is imported or solved, so
# this page stays free to render and has no cross-chapter value dependency.
# `create_chapter` deletes this page's freeze when it scaffolds a chapter,
# because rule 12 cannot -- the root index belongs to no chapter, so nothing
# else would notice a seventh node was missing.
#
# GRAPHVIZ, not mermaid. Quarto renders a ```{dot} block itself, so this costs
# no new dependency -- and `dot` lays out a TREE, which mermaid's default
# renderer did not do well enough to read. Drafted outside the notebook first,
# against a lineage with two branches in it, because the thing that decided it
# is what happens when this stops being a straight line: a hand-laid timeline
# drew three siblings as a straight continuation of one rail, which is a
# picture that LIES. `dot` gets it right without being told.
#
# ONE LABEL PER CHAPTER, and it is the change. A node's title and the change
# that produced it are the same fact here -- "3 mm foam" reached by "Changed to
# 3 mm foam" -- so the box carries the change and the title is the tooltip. A
# root has no change to name and carries its title, which is what it is: where
# the line started.
import pathlib
import re

_TITLE = re.compile(r'^title:\s*"(.+)"\s*$', re.M)


def _fork(_d):
    """`_fork.yml`'s parent and summary. Flat by design -- see lint.read_fork."""
    _f = _d / "_fork.yml"
    if not _f.exists():
        return None, ""
    _t = _f.read_text()
    _p = re.search(r"^parent:\s*(.+?)\s*$", _t, re.M)
    _s = re.search(r'^summary:\s*"?(.+?)"?\s*$', _t, re.M)
    return (_p.group(1).strip() if _p else None), (_s.group(1).strip() if _s else "")


_chapters = sorted(p for p in pathlib.Path("chapters").iterdir() if p.is_dir())
_titles, _parent, _label = {}, {}, {}
for _c in _chapters:
    _index = _c / "index.qmd"
    _m = _TITLE.search(_index.read_text()) if _index.exists() else None
    _titles[_c.name] = _m.group(1) if _m else _c.name
    # Only a parent that still exists: a fork naming a renamed chapter should
    # leave a root node rather than a dangling edge.
    _p, _s = _fork(_c)
    if _p and (pathlib.Path("chapters") / _p).is_dir():
        _parent[_c.name] = _p
        _label[_c.name] = _s.rstrip(".")

# A leaf is a chapter nothing was forked from: where a line of work reached.
_leaves = {c.name for c in _chapters} - set(_parent.values())
print("```{dot}")
print("//| fig-width: 5.2")
print("digraph lineage {")
print('  rankdir=TB; bgcolor="transparent"; ranksep=0.34; nodesep=0.22;')
print('  node [shape=box style="rounded,filled" fontname="Helvetica" '
      'fontsize=11 height=0.38 margin="0.22,0.09" penwidth=1.1];')
print('  edge [color="#bdc1c6" arrowsize=0.6 penwidth=1.1];')
for _c in _chapters:
    _head = _c.name in _leaves
    _text = _label.get(_c.name) or _titles[_c.name]
    print(f'  "{_c.name}" [label="{_text}" '
          f'URL="chapters/{_c.name}/index.html" tooltip="{_titles[_c.name]}" '
          f'fillcolor="{"#e8f0fe" if _head else "#ffffff"}" '
          f'color="{"#4285f4" if _head else "#dadce0"}" '
          f'fontcolor="{"#1a73e8" if _head else "#3c4043"}"];')
for _c in _chapters:
    if _c.name in _parent:
        print(f'  "{_parent[_c.name]}" -> "{_c.name}";')
print("}")
print("```")
```
